mathgap.title: Signed 'has N more than'
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly says 'X has N more than Y', translate it to X = Y + N (add N to Y).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Applicable when a statement explicitly mentions a numeric difference, e.g., 'X has 5 more than Y'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has N more than Y' as X = Y - N (subtracting instead of adding).

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: For a transfer statement 'X gives N to Y', subtract N from X's current count and add N to Y's current count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement describes a transfer of items from one person to another.
mathgap.example: Reversing the direction: adding N to X and subtracting N from Y.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a variable for each person, translate every statement into a linear equation (or inequality), and solve the resulting system.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the problem contains multiple interrelated statements that can be expressed as equations.
mathgap.example: Omitting a variable for a person, leading to an underdetermined system.

mathgap.title: Increase by factor interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'the number of X increases by k times', multiply the original amount by k to obtain the new amount.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any multiplicative increase phrasing such as 'increases by 2 times' or 'increases by 13/9 times'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'increase by k times' as adding k instead of multiplying.

mathgap.title: Equal split and redistribution handling
mathgap.principle: If a person splits all their items equally among a set of recipients, set the splitter's count to zero and give each recipient an equal share (original count divided by number of recipients). For redistribution between two people, combine their counts and split equally.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When statements involve splitting all items among others or redistributing between two parties to equalize.
mathgap.example: Giving each recipient the full original amount instead of dividing, or leaving the splitter with the original count.

mathgap.title: Signed difference phrasing
mathgap.principle: When a statement uses the phrase 'difference between X and Y' without qualifiers, treat it as the signed difference X - Y (order matters).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a relational statement mentions 'difference between' without 'absolute' or similar qualifiers.
mathgap.example: Treating 'difference between X and Y' as |X - Y| (absolute value) instead of X - Y.

mathgap.title: Sequential statement processing
mathgap.principle: Process the statements in the order given; direct count statements set the current count at that point, and later statements operate on those updated values.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains a sequence of actions (counts, transfers, conditionals) that depend on earlier updates.
mathgap.example: Applying a later transfer before an earlier count statement, violating the intended order.

mathgap.title: Signed 'has more than' in relational equations
mathgap.principle: When a relational statement says 'the number of X that Y has more than Z' (or similar) without a numeric amount, interpret it as a signed difference (X - Y) = ... rather than an absolute difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: In relational equations where a 'has more than' phrase appears without an explicit number.
mathgap.example: Treating 'X has more than Y' in an equation as |X - Y| instead of X - Y.

mathgap.title: Include transfers as constraints before solving relational equations
mathgap.principle: Treat each transfer as an equation linking the giver's and receiver's final counts, and incorporate these constraints before solving any relational equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a problem contains both transfer statements and relational equations linking counts.
mathgap.example: Solving relational equations first and only later applying transfer constraints, leading to inconsistent values.

mathgap.title: Direct counts as final constraints
mathgap.principle: When a problem includes both direct count statements (e.g., 'X has N items') and transfer statements, interpret the direct counts as describing the final amounts after all transfers, unless the text explicitly says otherwise.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count appears alongside transfers; treat the count as a final constraint and use transfers as equations linking final values.
mathgap.example: Treating 'X has N' as the initial amount before transfers, then applying transfers, which yields incorrect final totals.

mathgap.description: Treating 'X has N' as an initial count before transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes direct count statements describe the starting amounts, ignoring that the problem may define them as final amounts after transfers.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret direct count statements as final constraints unless the problem explicitly indicates they are initial; apply transfer equations to relate final counts.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often gives each recipient the full original amount or forgets to zero out the splitter, violating the equal division rule.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a person splits all items equally among recipients, set the splitter's count to zero and give each recipient original_count / number_of_recipients.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: Confusion between giver and receiver leads to adding to the giver and subtracting from the receiver.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: For 'X gives N to Y', subtract N from X and add N to Y.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has more than' in relational equations as absolute difference
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets the phrase as a magnitude rather than a signed difference, losing sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'has more than' in equations as a signed difference (X - Y), preserving sign.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'difference between X and Y' as absolute difference
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase is taken as |X - Y|, discarding the order of subtraction required by the problem.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'difference between X and Y' as X - Y (signed), respecting the order given.
